title: What Does the Bible Say About Witchcraft? 25 Verses
description: What the Bible says about witchcraft, sorcery, divination and mediums, from Deuteronomy 18 to Acts, with the verses in full.
keywords: what does the bible say about witchcraft
summary: Witchcraft is named in 5 verses of the World English Bible and sorcery in 22, and the words around them (divination, mediums, spells, omens) bring the total close to 50 verses. The Law forbids divination, sorcery, interpreting omens, casting spells and consulting mediums in one list (Deuteronomy 18:9-14) and sets death for a medium (Leviticus 20:27). The New Testament lists witchcraft among the works of the flesh (Galatians 5:19-20), records Simon the sorcerer (Acts 8:9-24), Elymas (Acts 13:6-11) and Ephesian converts burning their magic books (Acts 19:18-19), and places sorcerers outside the new Jerusalem (Revelation 21:8, 22:15). The verses below follow those passages.

faqs.q: Is witchcraft a sin in the Bible?
faqs.a: Yes. Deuteronomy 18:10-12 calls anyone who practices divination, sorcery or casting spells an abomination to the Lord, and Galatians 5:19-21 includes witchcraft among the works of the flesh. Revelation 21:8 lists sorcerers among those outside the city of God.

faqs.q: What does the Bible say about a witch?
faqs.a: Exodus 22:18 in the King James Version says not to suffer a witch to live. The World English Bible renders the Hebrew as 'a sorceress' and does not use the word witch at all (0 verses), while the King James uses it in 2. The verse sat inside Israel's civil law and has been read very differently across history.

faqs.q: What happened to Simon the sorcerer?
faqs.a: He amazed Samaria with magic, believed and was baptized, then offered money for the power to give the Holy Spirit. Peter told him his heart was not right before God and to repent (Acts 8:9-24).

faqs.q: Are tarot cards and horoscopes covered by these verses?
faqs.a: The Bible does not name them. Passages against divination, omens and consulting the stars (Deuteronomy 18:10-11, Isaiah 47:12-14) are the verses Christians apply to them.
